nodes.name: 1st of the month, 07:00 Brussels
nodes.notes: Runs at 07:00 on the 1st of every month. The workflow timezone is set to Europe/Brussels in Settings (below), so 07:00 is Antwerp time.

nodes.name: GET /api/cron/monthly-sales-report
nodes.notes: No ?month → the app builds the PREVIOUS calendar month. The app reads the database (read-only), puts ONLY the PDF in Drive and emails the HTML with the PDF attached to MONTHLY_SALES_REPORT_RECIPIENTS. neverError + full response so a 401/500 reaches the check below instead of silently stopping the run. onError = continue, so a timeout, DNS failure or refused connection (the app is down) also reaches the check and triggers the alert.

nodes.name: PDF in Drive and email sent?
nodes.notes: Success = HTTP 200 AND the PDF landed in Drive AND the email went out (or no recipients are configured yet, which is deliberate).

parameters.subject: =⚠️  LoveLab monthly sales report — not fully delivered ({{ $json.body?.month || 'unknown month' }})
parameters.message:
=

Monthly sales report — delivery problem

HTTP status: {{ $json.statusCode || 'no answer (app down, timeout or network error)' }}

  • Month: {{ $json.body?.month || '—' }}
  • Google Drive (PDF): {{ $json.body?.drive?.ok ? 'OK — ' + $json.body.drive.webViewLink : 'NOT uploaded — ' + ($json.body?.drive?.error || $json.body?.drive?.reason || '—') }}
  • Email (HTML + PDF): {{ $json.body?.email?.sent ? 'sent' : 'NOT sent — ' + ($json.body?.email?.error || $json.body?.email?.reason || '—') }}

App error, if any: {{ $json.body?.error || $json.error?.message || $json.error || '—' }}

Common causes: 401 = CRON_SECRET credential wrong; 404 = the report code is not deployed yet; 500 “No Chrome/Chromium” = Chromium missing on the server; Drive “env_not_set” = GOOGLE_DRIVE_SALES_REPORTS_FOLDER_ID missing. Re-run a month by hand: GET /api/cron/monthly-sales-report?month=YYYY-MM with the same header.

nodes.name: Email alert (delivery failed)
nodes.notes: Goes to N8N_SALES_REPORT_ALERT_TO, else N8N_ALERT_TO, else sam@love-lab.com (for now). Uses the existing Gmail OAuth2 credential — rename to match yours.
